blocks.text: Hattoo Singh's ordeal ends here when the second elephant did not crush Hattoo Singh either, further enraging Ahmad Shah. The ruler finally had him tied between two elephants and torn apart, presenting his death as a public martyrdom rather than a defeat in battle.

The page then turns to Episode About Bikaner, with Abdali still entrenched at Lahore while the Khalsa in Malwa struggled through want and accepted an invitation to aid Bikaner in its conflict with Jaisalmer. The Singhs fought effectively, but the Bikaner side broke faith and the Singhs were not paid the promised wages after the campaign was done.

Because the Khalsa could not make both ends meet under those conditions, the narrative explains why they began planning fresh raids for subsistence instead of remaining dependent on unreliable allies. The closing movement prepares the transition into the Bangar expedition by showing economic pressure, not greed, pushing the Singhs back into the field.
